name: AFC Bournemouth
summary: Formed in 1899 as Boscombe, the club became Bournemouth & Boscombe Athletic and has been AFC Bournemouth since 1971. For most of their history they were a lower-league side, entering administration in 1997 and 2008. Eddie Howe led them to three promotions in six years, and they reached the Premier League for the first time in 2015. They were relegated in 2020 and came straight back in 2022. In 2025–26 they finished sixth, their highest league finish, and qualified for the Europa League for the first time.

name: Arsenal
summary: Founded in 1886 by munitions workers at the Royal Arsenal in Woolwich as Dial Square, Arsenal were the first southern club to join the Football League (1893) and have been in the top division continuously since 1919. Herbert Chapman's 1930s side won five league titles, and under Arsène Wenger the club went unbeaten through the 2003–04 league season, earning the nickname 'The Invincibles'. They crossed London from Woolwich to Highbury in 1913 and moved to the Emirates Stadium in 2006. Arsenal were Premier League champions in 2025–26.

name: Aston Villa
summary: Founded in 1874, Aston Villa are one of England's oldest and most successful clubs: founder members of the Football League in 1888 (the idea came from Villa director William McGregor) and of the Premier League in 1992. They won seven league titles, the last in 1980–81, and the European Cup in 1981–82. Villa's only Premier League relegation came in 2015–16, and they returned in 2019. Under Unai Emery they reached the Champions League and won the Europa League in 2025–26.

stadiums.note: Largest football stadium in the English Midlands; has hosted 55 FA Cup semi-finals

name: Barnsley
summary: Founded in 1887 by Reverend Tiverton Preedy, Barnsley moved to Oakwell the following year and won the FA Cup in 1912 while a Second Division side. Their only Premier League season was 1997–98, after finishing second in the First Division, and they were relegated straight away. They have spent more seasons at English football's second level than any other club and now play in League One.

name: Birmingham City
summary: Formed in 1875 as Small Heath Alliance, the club became Small Heath in 1888, Birmingham in 1905 and Birmingham City in 1943. They were the first champions of the Football League Second Division and in 1960 became the first English club to reach a major European final (the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup). They won the League Cup in 1963 and 2011 and share the 'Second City derby' with Aston Villa. They now play in the Championship.

name: Blackburn Rovers
summary: Founded in 1875, Blackburn Rovers were founder members of the Football League in 1888 and won five FA Cups in the 19th century. Taken over by local businessman Jack Walker in 1991, who installed Kenny Dalglish as manager, they won promotion to the new Premier League in 1992 and became champions in 1994–95. They were relegated in 2012, dropped to the third tier in 2017, and returned to the Championship in 2018.

name: Blackpool
summary: Founded in 1887, Blackpool won the FA Cup in 1953 (the 'Matthews final', a 4–3 win over Bolton) and finished league runners-up in 1955–56. They became the first club to win promotion from every division of the Football League through the play-offs, reaching the Premier League in 2010. Their one Premier League season, 2010–11 under Ian Holloway, ended in relegation. They now play in League One.

name: Bolton Wanderers
summary: Formed in 1874 as Christ Church F.C. and renamed Bolton Wanderers in 1877, the club was one of the twelve founder members of the Football League in 1888. Bolton won the FA Cup four times (1923, 1926, 1929 and 1958); the 1923 final was the first ever held at Wembley, the 'White Horse Final'. They played in the Premier League for eleven straight seasons under Sam Allardyce, reaching the 2004 League Cup final, and have spent more seasons in the top flight than any other club without winning the league. Financial trouble led to administration in 2019, but they climbed back and won promotion to the Championship in 2026.

name: Bradford City
summary: Founded in 1903 and elected straight into the Football League, Bradford City won the Second Division in 1907–08 and the FA Cup in 1911, still their only major honour. They reached the Premier League in 1999, their first top-flight season in 77 years, and were relegated in 2001. Two administrations followed and they fell to the fourth tier before reaching the 2013 League Cup final. The club also suffered the Valley Parade fire of 11 May 1985, in which 56 supporters died. They now play in League One.

name: Brentford
summary: Founded in 1889, Brentford reached their highest league finish, fifth in the First Division, in 1935–36, then spent decades in the lower leagues. After promotion in 2014, they were promoted to the Premier League by winning the 2021 Championship play-off final, their first top-flight season since 1946–47. They left Griffin Park, their home since 1904, for a new stadium in 2020. Their main rivals are Fulham and Queens Park Rangers.

name: Brighton & Hove Albion
summary: Founded in 1901, Brighton spent most of the 20th century at the Goldstone Ground and played in the top flight from 1979 to 1983, reaching the 1983 FA Cup final. After the Goldstone was sold in 1997 the club nearly went out of the Football League and spent 14 years without a permanent home. Falmer Stadium opened in 2011, Brighton reached the Premier League in 2017, and in 2022–23 finished sixth, their best top-flight finish, to qualify for Europe for the first time. Their fiercest rivals are Crystal Palace.

name: Burnley
summary: Founded in 1882, Burnley were one of the first clubs to turn professional (1883) and one of the twelve founder members of the Football League. They have been English champions twice (1920–21 and 1959–60) and won the FA Cup in 1914, and are one of only five clubs to have won all four professional divisions. The 1959–60 title team came largely through the club's own youth system, making Burnley one of the smallest towns to produce a top-flight champion. They were relegated from the Premier League in 2025–26 and rival nearby Blackburn Rovers in the East Lancashire derby.

name: Cardiff City
summary: Founded in 1899 as Riverside A.F.C. and renamed Cardiff City in 1908, the Welsh club is the only team from outside England to have won the FA Cup, in 1927. They have also lost FA Cup finals in 1925 and 2008 and the 2012 League Cup final. Their most recent Premier League season was 2018–19, and they won promotion back to the Championship in 2026. They contest the South Wales derby with Swansea City.

name: Charlton Athletic
summary: Founded in 1905, Charlton won the FA Cup in 1947 and finished second in the First Division in 1936–37. They reached the Premier League by winning the 1998 play-off final, went straight back down, and then returned as First Division champions in 1999–2000 under Alan Curbishley, spending seven successive years in the top flight. Their history includes a long exile from The Valley: financial problems and safety concerns forced them to ground-share at Selhurst Park and then Upton Park before they returned in December 1992. They are now in the Championship.

name: Chelsea
summary: Chelsea were founded in 1905 specifically to play at Stamford Bridge, which they named themselves after the neighbouring area. They won their first league title in 1955 and their first Premier League title in 2004–05, and have since won two Champions Leagues (2012 and 2021) and the Europa League in 2013 and 2019. In 2025 they became the first club to win all of UEFA's men's club competitions. They have only ever had one home ground.

summary: Formed as Singers F.C. in 1883 and renamed Coventry City in 1898, the club won the FA Cup in 1987, still its only major trophy. Coventry spent 34 straight seasons in the top flight (1967–2001), including the first nine Premier League seasons, before sliding down to League Two by 2017. They climbed back, won the Championship in 2025–26, and return to the Premier League in 2026–27. They bought their stadium outright in August 2025 after a long rent dispute.

name: Crystal Palace
summary: Crystal Palace was formed as a professional club in 1905 to play in the FA Cup final stadium inside the Crystal Palace exhibition grounds. They finished third in the top flight in 1990–91, their best league finish, and were founder members of the Premier League. After relegation in 1998 and two spells in administration, they returned in 2013 and have played top-flight football ever since. They won the FA Cup in 2025, their first major trophy, and the Conference League in 2025–26. Their fiercest rivals are Brighton & Hove Albion.

name: Derby County
summary: Founded in 1884 as an offshoot of Derbyshire County Cricket Club, Derby were one of the twelve founder members of the Football League in 1888. They won the FA Cup in 1946 and the league title twice in the 1970s, reaching the European Cup semi-finals. They moved from the Baseball Ground to Pride Park in 1997, and are one of only nine clubs to have played in every season of the English league system. Their great rivals are Nottingham Forest in the East Midlands derby. They play in the Championship.

name: Everton
summary: Founded in 1878, Everton were founder members of both the Football League (1888) and the Premier League (1992), one of only three clubs to be both. They have won nine league titles, five FA Cups and the 1985 European Cup Winners' Cup, and have played more top-flight seasons than any other club, missing only four. The club left Anfield in 1892 after a rent dispute with landlord John Houlding, who then founded Liverpool. After 133 years at Goodison Park they moved to the new Hill Dickinson Stadium on the Liverpool waterfront in 2025. Their rivals are Liverpool in the Merseyside derby.

name: Fulham
summary: Founded in 1879 as St Andrews Cricket & Football Club, Fulham are London's oldest professional football club. They moved into Craven Cottage in 1896 and were elected to the Football League in 1907. Their best moments include the 1975 FA Cup final and, under Mohamed Al-Fayed's ownership from 1997, a rise to the Premier League by 2001, an Intertoto Cup win in 2002 and the 2010 Europa League final. Thirteen straight top-flight seasons ended in relegation in 2014; they have been back in the Premier League since 2022. Their West London derby rivals are Chelsea, Brentford and QPR.

name: Huddersfield Town
summary: Founded in 1908, Huddersfield won the FA Cup in 1922 and then three league titles in a row (1923–24, 1924–25 and 1925–26), the first two under Herbert Chapman. After falling to the fourth tier and nearly going out of business around 2003, they climbed back and won promotion to the Premier League in 2017 by beating Reading on penalties in the play-off final, making them the second club after Blackpool to have won all three divisional play-offs. They stayed up in 2017–18, were relegated in 2019, and now play in League One. They moved from Leeds Road to the Kirklees Stadium in 1994.

They lost the 2014 FA Cup final 3–2 to Arsenal after extra time. After dropping to the third tier in 2020 they were League One champions in 2020–21, and in 2026 won the play-off final against Middlesbrough to return to the Premier League. They moved from Boothferry Park to the KC Stadium (now the MKM Stadium) in 2002.

They also won the FA Cup in 1978 and the UEFA Cup in 1981. They have never lost at home in European competition. Their great rivals are Norwich City in the East Anglian derby. Under manager Don Revie in the 1960s and 1970s they won three top-flight league titles, the FA Cup, the League Cup and two Inter-Cities Fairs Cups. They have also been runners-up in the league five times and in the European Cup. Their rivals include Manchester United and Chelsea. They finished 14th in the Premier League in 2025–26.

summary: Founded in 1884 as Leicester Fosse and renamed Leicester City in 1919, the Foxes won the Premier League in 2015–16 at odds of 5000–1, one of seven clubs to have won the competition. They also won the FA Cup in 2021, the League Cup three times (1964, 1997 and 2000) and reached the Champions League quarter-finals in 2016–17. The club moved from Filbert Street to the Walkers Stadium, now the King Power Stadium, in 2002. They were relegated from the Championship in 2025–26 and play in League One.

They joined the Football League in 1893 and have played at Anfield ever since. They have won a joint-record twenty league titles, including the club's first in the Premier League era in 2020 under Jürgen Klopp and a twentieth in 2025 under Arne Slot, plus six European Cups. Their rivals are Everton in the Merseyside derby and Manchester United.

Financial collapse between 2007 and 2009 dropped them from the second tier to non-league football, but they climbed back and were promoted to the Premier League through the 2023 Championship play-offs. They spent one Premier League season (2023–24) and were relegated twice in a row, so they play in League One. A new stadium at Power Court is planned.

City won their first FA Cup in 1904 and had a successful spell under Joe Mercer and Malcolm Allison in the late 1960s and early 1970s. They dropped to the third tier for the only time in 1998 and have been in the Premier League since 2002–03. After Sheikh Mansour's 2008 takeover they won the Premier League in 2012 and, under Pep Guardiola (2016–2026), a first English domestic treble, a continental treble in 2023 and four consecutive league titles from 2020–21 to 2023–24.

name: Manchester United
summary: Founded in 1878 as Newton Heath LYR and renamed Manchester United in 1902, the club moved to Old Trafford in 1910. Matt Busby's 'Busby Babes' won titles in the 1950s before eight players died in the 1958 Munich air disaster, and United became the first English club to win the European Cup in 1968. Alex Ferguson (1986–2013) won 13 league titles, and in 1998–99 United became the first English side to win the Premier League, FA Cup and Champions League in one season. United share a joint-record twenty league titles with Liverpool and finished third in 2025–26.

name: Middlesbrough
summary: Formed in 1876, Middlesbrough were founder members of the Premier League in 1992. Their highest league finish is third (1913–14). The club nearly folded in 1986 before chairman Steve Gibson's consortium rescued it. Under Steve McClaren they won the League Cup in 2004, their first major trophy, and reached the 2006 UEFA Cup final. They lost both the FA Cup and League Cup finals in 1997, the same year they were relegated after a three-point deduction. They moved from Ayresome Park to the Riverside Stadium in 1995 and play in the Championship.

name: Newcastle United
summary: Founded in 1881 as Stanley F.C., the club became East End F.C. in 1882 and took the name Newcastle United in 1892 after absorbing the assets of the defunct Newcastle West End, including St James' Park. They have won four league titles, six FA Cups and the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, with their best period between 1904 and 1910. They have been in the Premier League for all but three seasons, were relegated in 2009 and 2016 and bounced straight back each time, and were bought by a Public Investment Fund-led consortium in 2021. In 2025 they won the League Cup, their first trophy in nearly 56 years. Their great rivals are Sunderland.

name: Norwich City
summary: Founded in 1902, Norwich have won the League Cup twice (1962 and 1985) and reached the 1958–59 FA Cup semi-final as a Third Division side. Their highest league finish was third in the inaugural 1992–93 Premier League season, and in the following season's UEFA Cup they became the only English club to beat Bayern Munich at the Olympiastadion. They moved to Carrow Road in 1935 and share the East Anglian derby with Ipswich Town. They play in the Championship.

name: Nottingham Forest
summary: Founded in 1865, Nottingham Forest are one of the oldest clubs in the world. Under Brian Clough and Peter Taylor they won back-to-back European Cups in 1979 and 1980, making Forest the only team in Europe to have won the European Cup more often than their domestic league title (they won it once). They have also won two FA Cups and four League Cups. Relegated in 1993, they returned immediately and finished third in 1995. They were relegated again in 1997 and 1999 and returned to the Premier League by winning the 2022 play-offs. Their rivals are Derby County in the East Midlands derby.

name: Oldham Athletic
summary: Founded in 1895 as Pine Villa, the club took the name Oldham Athletic when it moved to Boundary Park in 1899. They finished second in the First Division in 1914–15 and won the Second Division in 1990–91 under Joe Royle, which made them founder members of the Premier League in 1992 after 68 years out of the top flight. They were relegated in 1994 and in 2022 fell into the National League, becoming the first former Premier League club to play non-league football. They won back their Football League place via the 2025 National League play-off final and play in League Two.

name: Portsmouth
summary: Founded in 1898, Portsmouth were league champions in 1948–49 and 1949–50, won the FA Cup in 1939 and 2008, and held the FA Cup for a record seven years because the Second World War halted football. They spent seven years in the Premier League (2003 to 2010) before relegation, two spells in administration and three relegations. The club was bought by the Pompey Supporters Trust in 2013 and won League Two in 2016–17 and League One in 2023–24. They are one of only five clubs to have been champions of all four professional tiers, and the only English professional club not on mainland Great Britain. Their arch-rivals are Southampton.

name: Queens Park Rangers
summary: Founded in 1882 as Christchurch Rangers, the club took the name Queens Park Rangers in 1886 after merging with St Jude's Institute. QPR won the League Cup in 1967, their only major trophy, and finished just one point behind champions Liverpool in 1975–76. They were founder members of the Premier League in 1992 and went down in 1996, returning in 2011–12 and 2014–15 for a season each. They have been in the Championship since 2015. Their West London derby rivals are Chelsea, Fulham and Brentford.

summary: Founded in 1871, Reading are one of England's oldest clubs, though they only joined the Football League in 1920. They set a record of 106 points in the 2005–06 Championship and reached the Premier League for the first time in 2006–07, finishing eighth, their highest finish. They returned for 2012–13 and went down after one season. They reached the FA Cup semi-finals in 1927 and 2015. They moved from Elm Park to the Madejski Stadium in 1998 and play in League One.

name: Sheffield United
summary: Formed in 1889 as an offshoot of Sheffield United Cricket Club, the Blades have always played at Bramall Lane. They were English champions in 1897–98, won the FA Cup four times (1899, 1902, 1915 and 1925) and are one of only five clubs to have won all four professional divisions. They scored the first goal in Premier League history in 1992–93. Since then they have had several spells in the top flight, most recently in 2023–24. Their rivals are Sheffield Wednesday in the Steel City derby.

name: Sheffield Wednesday
summary: Formed in 1867 as an offshoot of The Wednesday Cricket Club, Sheffield Wednesday are the second-oldest professional association football club in England and were known as The Wednesday until 1929. They have won four league titles, three FA Cups and the League Cup, and in 1991 beat Manchester United in the League Cup final as a second-tier side, the last team to win a major English trophy while outside the top flight. Wednesday were founder members of the Premier League in 1992 but have not played top-flight football since 2000. They were relegated to League One in 2025–26.

name: Southampton
summary: Founded in 1885 as St. Mary's Y.M.A., a church team, Southampton won the FA Cup in 1976 as a Second Division side and finished First Division runners-up in 1983–84. They were Premier League founder members and stayed in the top flight until 2005, dropped to the third tier by 2009, and came back to the Premier League in 2012 for 11 years. They won promotion again through the 2024 play-off final but were relegated in April 2025. They moved from The Dell to St Mary's Stadium in 2001, and their rivals are Portsmouth.

name: Stoke City
summary: Founded as Stoke Ramblers (the club dates itself to 1863, with the first recorded match in 1868), Stoke were one of the twelve founder members of the Football League in 1888. Stanley Matthews made his debut in 1932. They won the League Cup in 1972, and under Tony Pulis spent ten years in the Premier League (2008 to 2018), reaching the 2011 FA Cup final. They moved from the Victoria Ground to the Britannia Stadium, now the bet365 Stadium, in 1997. Their local rivals are Port Vale and they play in the Championship.

summary: Formed in 1879 as Sunderland and District Teachers, the Black Cats have won six top-flight league titles (the last in 1936) and the FA Cup in 1937 and 1973. They played their first Premier League season in 1996–97, went down, and returned as First Division champions in 1999 with a then-record 105 points; Kevin Phillips won the European Golden Shoe with 30 goals. They left Roker Park for the Stadium of Light in 1997. Their fiercest rivals are Newcastle United in the Tyne–Wear derby. They were in the Premier League in 2025–26, finishing seventh.

name: Swansea City
summary: Founded in 1912 as Swansea Town and renamed Swansea City in 1970, the Welsh club climbed from the fourth tier to the top flight twice. In 2011 they became the first Welsh team in the Premier League, and in 2013 won the League Cup with a 5–0 win over Bradford City, the biggest win in a League Cup final, qualifying for the Europa League. They finished eighth in 2014–15, their best Premier League finish, and were relegated in 2018. They moved from the Vetch Field to the Liberty Stadium in 2005 and rival Cardiff City in the South Wales derby.

name: Swindon Town
summary: Founded in 1879 as Swindon AFC, the club became Spartans and then Swindon Town in 1883. They won the League Cup in 1969, beating Arsenal 3–1 while in the Third Division. After winning the 1990 Second Division play-off final they were denied promotion for breaching Football League rules, but Glenn Hoddle's side won the 1993 play-off final to reach the top flight for the first time. Their one Premier League season (1993–94) ended in relegation. They play in League Two.

name: Tottenham Hotspur
summary: Founded in 1882 as Hotspur F.C., Tottenham won the FA Cup in 1901 as a non-League club, and in 1960–61 became the first team of the 20th century to win the league and FA Cup double. In 1963 they were the first British club to win a European trophy, and in 1972 the inaugural UEFA Cup winners. They have won two league titles and eight FA Cups, and were Champions League runners-up in 2018–19. After 118 years at White Hart Lane they moved into the new Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in 2019, built on the same site. Their big rivals are Arsenal in the North London derby.

summary: Founded in 1881 as Watford Rovers, the Hornets rose from the fourth tier to the first under manager Graham Taylor between 1977 and 1987, finishing second in the First Division in 1982–83 and reaching the 1984 FA Cup final. They have had several Premier League spells: 1999–2000, 2006–07, 2015 to 2020 and 2021–22. They reached the 2019 FA Cup final but lost 6–0. Their rivals are nearby Luton Town. They play in the Championship.

name: West Bromwich Albion
summary: Formed in 1878, West Bromwich Albion were founder members of the Football League in 1888, won the league title in 1919–20 and have lifted the FA Cup five times (1888, 1892, 1931, 1954 and 1968). They also won the League Cup in 1966. Albion's last Premier League season was 2020–21. The Hawthorns, their home since 1900, is the highest of all 92 Premier League and Football League grounds, at 551 feet above sea level. Their traditional rivals are Aston Villa and Wolverhampton Wanderers, whom they meet in the Black Country derby.

name: West Ham United
summary: Founded in 1895 as Thames Ironworks and reformed as West Ham United in 1900, the club played at the Boleyn Ground (Upton Park) from 1904 until 2016, when it moved into the former Olympic Stadium, now the London Stadium. West Ham won the FA Cup in 1964, 1975 and 1980 and the European Cup Winners' Cup in 1965, and in 2023 won the Europa Conference League, their first major trophy since 1980. Their highest league finish was third in 1985–86. Bobby Moore, Geoff Hurst and Martin Peters were three of England's 1966 World Cup winners. They were relegated from the Premier League in 2025–26, and their long-standing rivals are Millwall.

After winning promotion in 2004–05 they spent eight seasons in the Premier League, and in 2013 beat Manchester City in the FA Cup final, but were relegated the same season. Administration in 2020 and repeated points deductions followed. They have won the League One title four times and play there now. Bolton Wanderers are their main derby rivals.

name: Wimbledon
summary: Founded in 1889 as Wimbledon Old Centrals, Wimbledon were a non-League club for most of their history until their election to the Football League in 1977. Their 'Crazy Gang' side rose from the Fourth Division to the First in four seasons, reaching the top flight in 1986, and won the 1988 FA Cup by beating champions Liverpool. They were founder members of the Premier League and stayed until relegation in 2000. After leaving Plough Lane in 1991 they ground-shared at Selhurst Park for twelve years, then moved to Milton Keynes in 2003, a move the FA approved against huge fan opposition. Supporters formed AFC Wimbledon in protest, and Wimbledon FC became Milton Keynes Dons when it was dissolved in 2004.

name: Wolverhampton Wanderers
summary: Formed in 1877 as St. Luke's F.C. and renamed Wolverhampton Wanderers in 1879, Wolves were founder members of the Football League in 1888. They were English champions three times (1953–54, 1957–58 and 1958–59) under Stan Cullis, and have won the FA Cup four times and the League Cup in 1974 and 1980. Their 1950s floodlit friendlies against overseas clubs helped inspire the European Cup. After a financial crisis in the 1980s they dropped to the Fourth Division, then climbed back, reaching the Premier League for the first time in 2003. They have played at Molineux since 1889, and their main rivals are West Bromwich Albion in the Black Country derby. They were relegated in 2025–26.
